lines.why: A flat forecast about the war itself, stated as belief with no argument attached; the war gear later contradicts it.
Files everyone warning of war as unserious before any of them has spoken; the reply is answered in advance.
Narrows the no-war forecast to a US war the moment Israel strikes, and treats the challenge as settled before weighing it.
An insult in place of an answer; nothing about the war is taken up.
Restates the war's state to win the exchange and still leaves the other side a way to answer: wake me up when that changes.
A wager on his own record, offered to the other side as the terms of the argument.
On the day the US bombs Iran the forecast is held by redefining war as boots on the ground; still arguing it out with the other side.
Tells the other side they have missed the picture instead of answering what they said about the strikes.
Describes his own side's record to rally it, in good faith, without attacking the reply.

patterns.phrase: personally invested in seeing the administration fail

lines.why: Assigns a motive to the war's critics before weighing their case, so their case need not be met.

patterns.phrase: all those big spaces and posts

lines.why: Mocks the warnings as a genre eight days after the US strikes, answering the warners before they can point at the strikes.
A bare declaration about the object's state, made after US strikes, held only by the narrowed meaning of war.
A rally line: the other side was wrong and look what we got instead; built to win the room, not to shut it.
Sets his own stake on the war's form, boots, as the test; a wager offered to the other side on narrowed terms.
A statement of what matters most to him; not about the war, no argument aimed at anyone.
Reclassifies the people listed as the enemy on one axis, so nothing they say about the war needs an answer.
On the war's first day the object is measured by boots; still arguing the point against the people calling it a war.
Calls the other side liars chasing headpats, answering their motive instead of their claim.
States his own view of the war's conduct and leaves it open: we have to see how this plays out.
The same narrowed measure of the war, stated flat, as the setup for the line that follows.

patterns.phrase: even if there were, I don't care anymore

lines.why: Settles his own wager in advance whatever happens and spends his own standing to do it; the war is traded for one loyalty.
His own record restated as his own words, so it is scored as his; it rewrites the mockery of June as skepticism, while still making a case to the room.

patterns.phrase: the price one pays for nuance

lines.why: Files the replies as a failure to handle nuance before meeting any of them.

patterns.phrase: All these people do is lie

lines.why: Calls the other side liars wholesale and talks over them, as in the ruled case on the same speaker.
Takes the war as happening and states a plain wish about it; no one is argued with.
Makes his case on the war's form and dates his record back to always, which the set does not show.
A plain reading of the object's state six months into the war, measured by invasion rather than war.

patterns.phrase: opposed the Iran war from the outset

lines.why: Describes his own record to win BAP back, as in the ruled case; the record is revised to opposition from the outset.
Answers BAP's charge directly and appeals to him; the exchange stays open.
An appeal to what BAP already knows about him, to keep him on side.

moments.why: When Israel goes to war with Iran he refuses the plain reading of his own no-war forecast by narrowing war to a US war.
He had offered to eat his words when things changed; on the day the US bombs Iran he refuses the change by redefining war as boots on the ground.
Wake me up when that changes was the term; after the US strikes on the nuclear sites he declares no war rather than waking.
He settles his own boot wager early: even if there were boots, he no longer cares, so the test he set is refused before it can be applied.
He takes up skepticism of the strikes, the very reading he mocked in June as big spaces and posts.
He accepts the war as happening, the thing he said was simply not in the cards, and asks only that it end quickly.
He refuses his own July record, no war with Iran and thank you Trump, and replaces it with opposition from the outset.
